clue.text: Lord Peter, they say, caught a criminal in the end — fantastic!

indicators.note: what people say is heard rather than read, so the name is taken for its pronunciation
in the end points to the final position of the word it follows, so only its closing letter counts

blocks.note: Lord Peter Wimsey is Dorothy L. Sayers's aristocratic detective; his surname is pronounced like the start of a word for fancifulness
c. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written
the closing letter of criminal

explanation.surface: A gleeful report that the aristocratic sleuth has finally nabbed the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic!' reads as a cheer at the arrest, but it is the definition. Wimsey's name supplies the sound of WHIMSI, then C, A and L complete WHIMSICAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic in its older sense means fanciful or capricious, which is exactly what a whimsical idea or design is.

clue.text: Attacking wingers in striped jerseys

blocks.note: surface reading: rugby or football wide men going forward in hooped kit
setter's reading: winged insects with black and yellow stripes that sting when they attack

explanation.walkthrough: Wingers sounds like sport, and Wasps is in fact a London rugby club, but the real wingers are insects with striped bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps are stinging winged insects whose bodies are banded yellow and black, as if dressed in a striped shirt.

clue.text: Follow copy

blocks.note: first meaning: take as a model, as in following someone's example
second meaning: reproduce or mimic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Follow copy' looks like a printer's instruction to stick to the text; the two words are separate synonyms of one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to model behaviour on another person's, which is both following them and copying them.

clue.text: Go easy, having often put one's foot down about a student

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for speeding up is wrapped around the word for frequently

blocks.note: to put one's foot down on the accelerator is to go faster
oft is the poetic form of often
taken as written
L for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: Told to be gentle after often stamping one's foot over some student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's foot down' suggests being firm, the opposite of going easy; here it is a driver pressing the accelerator. L for learner is the usual crossword student.
explanation.definitionFit: To soft-pedal is to play down or treat with restraint, from the piano pedal that softens the sound.

clue.text: A rush to fix the light-holder

blocks.note: a rush, or rushlight, is a cheap candle made from the pith of a rush dipped in fat
to stick something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying to repair the lampstand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rush' reads as a hurry; here it is the rushlight, an old kind of cheap candle.
explanation.definitionFit: A candlestick is a holder with a socket for a candle, so it literally holds a light.

clue.text: See the bachelor making a highball

definitions.note: a verb: to send a ball high

blocks.note: lo is an archaic exclamation meaning look or see
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: Watching an unmarried man mix himself a whisky and soda.
explanation.walkthrough: Highball sounds like the cocktail, but here it is a ball hit high into the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A lob is a stroke in tennis or cricket that sends the ball up in a high arc over an opponent.

clue.text: Drops trousers

blocks.note: first meaning: lowers the head or body quickly, as to avoid a blow
second meaning: light trousers made of heavy cotton or linen cloth

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue suggests someone dropping their trousers; the two words are separate meanings. Ducks are white canvas trousers, as once worn by sailors and cricketers.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck is to bob down suddenly, and ducks are also plural garments cut from a strong untwilled cotton fabric.

clue.text: Medico with pointed instrument affected speech

blocks.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, and a medico is a doctor
an awl is a pointed tool for piercing leather or wood

explanation.surface: A doctor brandishing something sharp while talking in a put-on voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, lengthened manner of speaking, often an affected or mannered one.

clue.text: Sign of a storm about record of progress in German city

indicators.note: about means around, so the warning signal surrounds the word for a record

blocks.note: a storm cone is a canvas cone hoisted at British coastguard stations to warn of gales
a ship's log records the progress of a voyage

explanation.surface: A weather warning raised around a progress report in a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: A storm cone is a canvas cone hoisted at British coastguard stations to warn shipping of gales; a ship's log records the progress of a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne, or Köln, is a large city on the Rhine in western Germany, famous for its cathedral.

clue.text: Disguise protects a witness

indicators.note: to disguise something is to alter its appearance, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in disguise shields a witness, like a police protection scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The protected-witness picture misleads: witness is the definition in its sense of onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event, and a witness in the general sense is anyone who sees something happen.

clue.text: Pompous English name for starch

blocks.note: stiff can describe formal, pompous manners
E is the standard abbreviation for English
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A grand-sounding English term for the laundry product starch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starch' looks like a noun here, but it is a verb: what starch does to a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: To starch a shirt collar is to make it rigid, so the verb is a synonym for making something firm.

clue.text: Writing in relief to the Liberal Assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together into a new structure, so the letters of the word before it are built into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written; seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A letter of thanks sent to the annual conference of the Liberal Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal Assembly' reads as the name of a party conference, but Assembly is the anagram signal working on Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Braille is the system of raised dots read by touch, a script embossed on the page rather than printed flat.

clue.text: Note introduction of stringed instrument

indicators.note: an introduction is what comes first, so only the opening letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of stringed
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A memo about the opening of a string instrument, or the first note it plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stringed instrument' reads as one phrase, but stringed only gives its first letter and instrument alone gives the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp is a musical note raised by a semitone, as in F sharp, so it names a kind of note.

clue.text: Illumination for bookcase

blocks.note: surface reading: lighting fitted to a piece of library furniture
setter's reading: a case in a book, worked on by a detective reading late into the night under a lamp

explanation.surface: Lighting fitted over a set of shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is one cryptic definition: bookcase hides a case to be read or solved, and the soft glow of a lamp is what one reads by.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamplight is the glow from an oil or electric lamp, the traditional illumination for reading or study in the evening.

clue.text: Controller's job is to make the island on time with the royal yacht

blocks.note: the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea
an age is a period of time
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
a yacht is a kind of ship

explanation.surface: An official's task is to get to the island in time to meet the royal yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above. The island is the Isle of Man; the surface hints at Britannia, the royal yacht, but yacht just means a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager controls a business or team, and managership is the post or office that such a person holds.

clue.text: Go to court a girl

blocks.note: first meaning: bring a legal action against someone
second meaning: a woman's first name

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests courting a girl romantically; court is really the law court, and the girl is just a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to take legal proceedings, and it is also a short form of the female name Susan.

clue.text: A toady we may have to copy? Shan't!

indicators.note: suggests the letters that follow may be made into something else by rearranging them

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A flatterer is expected to imitate the boss, and someone refuses: shan't!
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is loose: the setter says the toady is something we may get from these words, and the surface's refusal to copy is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fawns on the powerful to gain favour, which is exactly what a toady does.

clue.text: Freedom from involvement is to a girl's advantage

blocks.note: Di is a short girl's name; with the possessive it is Di's
to act in someone's interest is to act to their advantage

explanation.surface: Staying out of an affair turns out to benefit some young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, 'to a girl's advantage' is 'in Di's interest', which runs together as DISINTEREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterest in its strict sense is impartiality: having no personal stake or involvement in the matter at hand.

clue.text: Both parts of Ireland united against peace plan

blocks.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic, and NI is Northern Ireland
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: North and South of Ireland joining in opposition to a proposed settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' reads as Irish reunification; it just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An eirenicon, from the Greek for peaceful, is a proposal made to reconcile opposing parties, especially in religious disputes.

clue.text: Wait for girl vocalist

blocks.note: a common female first name
a vocalist is a singer

explanation.surface: Hanging about until a female singer turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: the waits were bands of musicians who went from house to house at Christmas singing carols.
explanation.definitionFit: In British tradition the Christmas waits are groups of street musicians and singers going door to door with seasonal songs.

clue.text: Seed here falls upon stony ground

definitions.text: Seed here falls upon stony ground

blocks.clueFragment: Seed here falls upon stony ground
blocks.note: surface reading: the parable of the sower, where seed on stony ground withers
setter's reading: a garden feature built of stones where seeds are sown among the rocks on purpose

explanation.walkthrough: The Gospel parable says seed on stony ground fails; here the stony ground is a deliberately built garden bed of rocks and alpine plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is a garden area of piled stones and soil planted with alpines, so seeds there land among stones.

clue.text: Reverse thrust causing damage

indicators.note: reverse means run backwards, so the following word is read from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: to ram is to thrust or drive forcefully

explanation.surface: A jet's reverse thrust on landing doing harm to the aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse thrust' is a real aviation term, which hides that Reverse is an instruction applied to thrust.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or impair it, a straightforward synonym for doing it harm.

clue.text: Graduate volunteers to receive information from the battlefield

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so the volunteers hold the information inside

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Volunteers with a degree are briefed on what is happening at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is unusual: the colour is named after the Battle of Magenta of 1859, so the word comes from a battlefield. TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta, the purplish-red dye, took its name from the Italian town where the French and Sardinians beat Austria in 1859.

clue.text: It helps the sick at heart to carry on

definitions.text: It helps the sick at heart to carry on

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who comforts the miserable and keeps their spirits up

blocks.clueFragment: It helps the sick at heart to carry on
blocks.note: setter's reading: a medical device that keeps a diseased heart beating regularly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick at heart' is an idiom for sad, but here it means literally having heart disease, and 'carry on' means keep the heart going.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacemaker is an implanted electronic device that regulates the heartbeat of patients with cardiac rhythm disorders.

clue.text: Proposed troop-leader is under 24

indicators.note: in a down clue being under means placed below, so the leader comes after the other piece

blocks.note: the answer to 24 across is a synonym of mean
the first letter of troop

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the scout troop's leader is younger than twenty-four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under 24' looks like an age limit; 24 refers to the answer at 24 across, whose synonym MEAN sits above T.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is a past participle of mean in its sense of intend, so what was meant was what was proposed or intended.

clue.text: Paperback about, say, the emperor

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned word goes around the next one

blocks.note: read as paper + back: The Sun, a British daily newspaper, taken backwards
e.g. means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.surface: A cheap paperback edition about the ruler, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paperback' looks like one word for a cheap book; it splits into paper and back, and The Sun is the usual crossword paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus was the title of the emperor or king of Ethiopia, borne for example by Haile Selassie.

clue.text: Full title is in fashion

blocks.note: first meaning: the complete formal designation of a person, as a noun
second meaning: elegance or fashionable flair

explanation.surface: A grand formal title has become the latest trend.
explanation.walkthrough: One's style is one's full formal title, as in 'His Royal Highness'; 'in style' means fashionably.
explanation.definitionFit: A style is the official form of address of a dignitary, and fashion and style are near synonyms for current taste.

clue.text: A typical hailstorm

definitions.note: with its article: an average one is a typical one

blocks.note: the hail half: ave is the Latin greeting, a hail
the storm half: a storm of anger is a rage

explanation.surface: An ordinary hailstorm, nothing unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hailstorm' looks like one weather word, but splits into hail and storm, each with its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Average describes what is usual or ordinary, the normal standard that a typical example represents.

clue.text: Knock five off a girl's age

indicators.note: to knock something off is to remove it, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
a common female first name

explanation.surface: Taking five years off a woman's real age.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about lying about age, but five is the Roman V removed from the start of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, and age is used for the same thing, as in the Iron Age.

clue.text: Sort of horse and carriage

blocks.note: first meaning: a breed of high-stepping trotting horse
second meaning: a horse-drawn coach kept for hire

explanation.surface: A horse and carriage, as in the old song.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as horse and carriage together, but each is a separate meaning of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hackney is a British breed of carriage horse, and a hackney carriage is the old and official name for a hired cab.

clue.text: Seek a way to get an appointment

blocks.note: to try for something is to seek it
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Looking for some route to secure a meeting with someone busy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a prearranged meeting, typically a secret rendezvous between lovers, so it is a romantic sort of appointment.

clue.text: A couple of pawns, with time about to expire, take an additional piece

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the chess notation for a pawn, so two of them
something about to expire is coming to its end
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A chess player short on the clock sacrifices two pawns to win an extra piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: pawns, time and pieces all suggest the game, but each just supplies letters, and 'piece' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added or attached to a larger whole, such as a limb or a supplementary part.
